newsitem.title: FRANCE: Marseille air cargo traffic up 11.9pct in October.
newsitem.headline: Marseille air cargo traffic up 11.9pct in October.

text.p: Marseille-Provence airport said it handled 3,946 tonnes of air cargo traffic last month, an increase of 11.9 percent on October 1995.
Strong growth in cargo volumes transported by French airline, L'Aeropostale, was one of the main reasons for the increase, an airport authority official told Reuters.
Air cargo traffic was also swelled by two ad hoc Antonov 124 flights from Marseille to Yemen which carried 162 tonnes of electrical equipment.
The flights were charted by forwarding agents, Panalpina and operated by Heavylift, the official said.
In the first ten months of 1996, throughput at France's second biggest gateway for airfreight (after the Paris airports) totalled 36,416 tonnes, up one percent on the same period last year.

"After a poor first few months of the year, we have now achieved overall growth in air cargo traffic on 1995 levels and our estimates for the first two weeks of November show that this trend has continued," the official added.

January-October 1996 postal traffic handled at Marseille totalled 16,816 tonnes, an increase of 6.6 percent on 1995 levels, the official added. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
